what: Medline is the largest supplier of medical and surgical products in the United States. It manufactures its own gloves, gowns, drapes, wound care and exam supplies, and also runs the distribution network that delivers them to hospitals.
customers: Hospitals, surgery centres, physician offices, nursing homes and home care providers.
money: its own manufactured medical and surgical products
distribution of its own and third-party products to care settings
moat: Owning both the products and the distribution network, so it can guarantee supply when hospitals most need it, backed by long-term contracts with hospital groups.
risks: Net margin of about 4% is thin, as is normal in distribution
Debt of about $13 billion remains from the private equity buyout before its listing
Hospital cost pressure limits price increases
Tariffs raise the cost of products made abroad
opportunities: Its own-brand products earn far more than distributing other companies' goods
Hospitals increasingly want a single supplier that can guarantee supply after pandemic shortages
watch: Medline Brand revenue as a share of the total, and operating margin.
